To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
compiler-based approaches can be very successful in reducing power consumption for array intensive embedded applications running on multi processor, NoCs.

the compiler-based approach can reduce the power consumption of on-chip networks by up to 30% and that the compiler-based channel turn-off scheme can outperform the hardware based scheme by up to 40%.

compiler-based channel reuse optimization reduces power consumption of array-intensive applications by 40% to 80% and that it is a very effective approach for power reduction in on-chip network based embedded systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of compiler-based techniques to reduce power consumption of applications running on emerging multi-processor, NoC based embedded systems.
the design of compiler technology that can be used to optimize the communication patterns of array-intensive embedded applications for power savings.
the development of a compiler-based technique that can significantly reduce power consumption of embedded applications running on multi-processor systems with on-chip communication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the compiler based approach can save 30% of power consumption in the network on average while the performance loss is only 1.2%.
the proposed compiler approach is a very effective way of saving power in NoC based embedded systems.
the proposed approach can reduce the average power consumption by up to 50%, while increasing the average communication latency by less than 1%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
compiler technology is a key enabler for power reduction in emerging on-chip networks.

the power savings obtained by compiler-directed channel reuse are very significant, and the proposed approach is a promising technique to be used by the compiler to reduce power consumption in future embedded systems.

the compiler-based approach can be used to significantly reduce the energy consumption of NoC based embedded systems.
